easy.def: A word that shows where something goes.
examples: We walk to school.
I gave the ball to Mia.
The bus goes to the zoo.

more.def: A word that shows the place, person, or thing that something moves toward or is aimed at.
examples: The train travels from the city to the coast.
She wrote a letter to her grandfather.
Please listen to the instructions carefully.
I am home today.
It is sunny today.
We have art today.

more.def: On this present day, or at the present time.
examples: Today our class is visiting the science museum.
I planted the seeds today, and I hope they grow.
Many people today use phones to take photographs.
We play together.
They walked together.
Let us sing together.

more.def: With each other, or at the same time or place.
examples: The whole family cooked dinner together.
Put the two pieces together to make a puzzle.
The geese flew south together in a long line.
We go tomorrow.
See you tomorrow.
It will snow tomorrow.
Our class is going to the zoo tomorrow.
I will return the library book tomorrow.
Tomorrow will be warm and sunny.
We eat pizza tonight.
I sleep early tonight.
It will be cold tonight.

more.def: During the night that is coming, or this evening.
examples: The moon will be full tonight, so look out the window.
We are having soup and bread for dinner tonight.
My grandparents are coming to visit tonight.
I want to come too.
She likes pizza too.
Can I play too?

more.def: Also, or in addition to something that was just said.
examples: My brother plays the drums, and my sister plays them too.
I would like some juice too, please.
Frogs are amphibians, and toads are too.
The soup is too hot.
This box is too big.
It is too late.

more.def: More than is needed, wanted, or allowed.
examples: The coat was too small, so I gave it to my cousin.
It is too dark to read without a lamp.
Do not eat too much candy before dinner.

easy.def: A storm with wind that spins very fast.
examples: The tornado spun across the field.
We go to the basement in a tornado.
The tornado looked like a big gray cone.

more.def: A powerful storm with a spinning, funnel-shaped column of wind.
examples: The family hid in the basement until the tornado passed.
The tornado tore the roof off the barn.
A siren warns the town when a tornado is near.

easy.def: A place where many people live, smaller than a city.
examples: I live in a small town.
We went to town.
The town has a park.

more.def: A place where people live and work, bigger than a village and smaller than a city.
examples: Our town has a library, a bakery, and a park.
The whole town came to watch the parade.
We drove into town to buy groceries.
